author: haiku
label: seeded-01-01
changes: Added a terms section defining billing_mode, shadow store, comparison_results, mismatch, rollback record and usage event log.
Replaced the loose notes with a list of what each mode does, so each engine's role is explicit.
Spelled out the forward gates and the nightly comparison job, including what a mismatch is and what each night counts as.
Rewrote rollback: start points, the two triggers, the five steps in order, and which steps are skipped from shadow and both.
Added the rollback record and the rule that each step must be safe to retry, replacing the bare note that steps are retryable.
Defined the gate reset: the day count, Finance sign-off, and what happens to comparison_results.
Added a failure table for a failed or hung step, a charge-failure spike, and shadow errors.
Stated the 35-day clock and its start point, and that day 35 ends the way back.
Added labels to the forward transitions and made decommission depend on day 35, so the diagram matches the text. Put the rollback steps in the diagram, and the skip rules in the text.
Added an open questions section for the 5,000-invoice count, the failure-rate denominator and the maximum pause length.
Added that both engines read the same usage event log, with no second copy (Q11).
Reconcile now says where the due amount and the charged amount come from, and that it checks the ledger before each charge (Q12).
Named the rollback runner as the retrier, added the hung-versus-slow rule, and made on-call the handoff when retries run out (Q13).
Added the one-rollback-at-a-time rule, with a second trigger logged and not started (Q14).
Defined a resolved mismatch as the newest comparison_results row having no flag, and said the nightly job clears it on a matching night (Q15).
Made decommissioning a person's decision, with the gate stated, and made rollback refused from day 35 on (Q16).
Replaced the per-step skip notes with one table of which steps run from each starting mode, which also shows that resume_charging is skipped from shadow.
Stated that the rollback record lists only the steps that apply to its starting mode.
Stated that after a rollback the forward path restarts at shadow, as the brief requires.
Reorganised the document into summary, terms, diagram, modes and state, forward moves, rollback, failures, decommissioning and open questions. Removed repeated statements of the same rules.
Added open questions for in-flight charges, a ledger total above the due amount, retry limits, and failures after day 35.
Kept the brief's Mermaid diagram form, and added the day-35 limit to the rollback-from-new_only edge.
Moved the summary and terms to the top, ahead of the diagram, and put the mode notes and state locations just after it, as step 7 asks.
Cut the sentence that says the diagram shows the same steps as the rollback table. The table and diagram are already consistent.

Merged the separate 'Modes and where state lives' and 'Forward moves' sections into one mode list plus one list of forward moves, each with the same parts (starts, gate or action, data, what happens on failure).
Merged the 'A person sets billing_mode, the controller refuses unless the gate has passed' rule, which was stated in three places, into the forward-moves section only.

Merged the rollback steps into a single list where each step has the same parts (starts, what it does, data, what happens on failure). The starting-mode table is kept, since it is the spec for which steps run.
Merged the two failure tables into one table, adding the forward-move refusal and the step failure rows that were only in the rollback text.
Stated the 'each step is safe to run twice' and 'a retry skips done steps' rules once, instead of in both the steps and the retry text.
Cut the repeated day-35 explanation from the rollback text. The rule now appears once in the decommissioning section and once in the failure table.
Split the nightly comparison into its own short section with the same parts as the other steps, so the gates' data source is clear.
Kept all eight open questions unchanged. None was answered, because the brief does not decide them and no decision was invented.
Kept the Mermaid diagram unchanged, because a diagram keeps its form.
